question: Should OpenClaw core support native per-task model hints in HEARTBEAT.md, or should heartbeat model routing remain per-turn and plugin-owned unless a missing generic seam is proven?
rationale: Current main lacks the requested task-level boundary, but adding it would create public HEARTBEAT.md syntax and model/session precedence rules; the existing before_model_resolve hook covers whole-turn routing but not exact per-task escalation.

options.title: Keep routing plugin-owned for now
options.body: Document that heartbeat ticks are routed as one model-selected turn and use before_model_resolve or ClawHub plugins for routing policy unless maintainers approve native task splitting.

options.title: Add native task model hints
options.body: Define model/provider task fields, split or group due tasks by effective model, and add docs/tests for precedence, timestamps, and shared-session restoration.

options.title: Fold into scheduled-job routing
options.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/42631 as the canonical scheduled model-override track and avoid a separate heartbeat-specific routing syntax until cron and heartbeat semantics converge.

recommendation.title: Keep routing plugin-owned for now
recommendation.body: Document that heartbeat ticks are routed as one model-selected turn and use before_model_resolve or ClawHub plugins for routing policy unless maintainers approve native task splitting.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision is primarily about product boundary between core HEARTBEAT.md syntax and plugin-owned model routing, and steipete introduced the current model-resolution hook seam.
